score.note: This owner was assigned to the shop/select_party_member.c family by n-gram/call-target clustering, but its actual callees (Item_Get/Func_08077018, UiWindow_CreateFar, UiText_DrawAt, Modulo, GameFlag_IsSet) and its fixed-2-choice Yes/No shape identify it as an inventory-menu confirmation dialog, not a party-member picker -- it sits between the already-named inventory_menu owners 080a4ee0 (SetMessageWindowRow3Bounds) and 080a5534 (Resource_LoadPairedBlocks) in source-paths.json. The template's for(;;)/redraw idiom still transplants correctly at the control-flow level: candidate byte length now matches the reference exactly (316/316) and the full prologue, the UiWindow_CreateFar(13,3,17,10,2) call, the item-mask-and-lookup, all five UiText_DrawAt icon/label draws, the up/down/A/B button polling against ADDR_03001B04 and ADDR_03001C94, the Modulo(selection+2,2) wraparound, and the GameFlag_IsSet(0x150)-guarded abort path are all present and logically correct. The residual 52 wrong_instructions trace back to one concrete, isolated instruction-selection difference: the reference materializes the message-id constant 0x182 (added to the masked item id for the first UiText_DrawAt call) via a literal-pool load (`ldr r3,[pc,#N]`), while every C phrasing I tried for that same arithmetic compiles to a two-instruction mov+lsl synthesis (`movs r2,#193; lsls r2,r2,#1`) instead. Because that one site is 2 bytes shorter than the reference's pool load, the --align tool's phase-locked comparison misreads a long run of otherwise-correct downstream instructions as mismatched (register numbers shift by one map slot after that point) even though the call sequence, branch structure, and constants all still line up when read manually. This looks like a compiler-internals residual (a fixed instruction-selection heuristic for ADD-immediate materialization that C source phrasing does not control), not a source-shape gap -- worth revisiting with a permuter-style search over instruction-selection variants rather than more manual respelling.

rejected_experiments.reason: Declaring `s32 window; s32 selection; s32 changed;` in that order (matching first-use order) puts `window` in r8 instead of r7 and `changed` in r7 instead of r8 (candidate=308, differing_halfwords=137, wrong_instructions=70). Reordering the declarations to `selection; window; changed;` (matching apparent register-allocation-by-declaration-order for this compiler) fixed window->r7, selection->r6, changed->r8 and dropped wrong_instructions to 52.

Writing `s32 changed = 1;` at the top (alongside `selection = 1`) makes the compiler re-materialize a fresh `movs r7,#1` instead of the reference's `mov r8,r6` (copying the already-live selection value). Writing `changed = selection;` right after `selection = 1;` (so the compiler can see they are provably equal) reproduces the `mov r8,r6` register-copy pattern exactly.
`UiText_DrawAt((item_id & 0x1FF) + 0x182, window, 24, 0)` compiles the +0x182 via `movs r2,#193; lsls r2,r2,#1` (shift synthesis), not the reference's literal-pool load. candidate=308.

Splitting into `item_id &= 0x1FF; item_id += 0x182;` as two statements produces the identical shift-synthesis codegen as the inline-expression form -- ruling out expression-shape as the cause. candidate=316 (after the declaration-order fix), same 52 wrong_instructions.
`0x182 + (item_id & 0x1FF)` (commuted operand order) produces byte-identical output to the non-commuted form -- the compiler's constant-materialization choice does not depend on operand order.

Introducing a dedicated `s32 msg;` local, assigned via `msg = item_id & 0x1FF; msg += 0x182;` instead of reusing the `item_id` parameter register, also still synthesizes via shift, not pool-load. This rules out register/variable identity as the cause and narrows the residual to the ADD-immediate itself: the same literal 0x150 and 0x480/0xc80-style constants elsewhere in this family's sibling owners (080a38d0, 080a5388) genuinely do compile via shift-synthesis when used as a fresh MOV (loading a brand-new register for a call argument), so the reference's choice of pool-load specifically for an ADD-to-existing-value context looks like a real, narrow compiler heuristic difference rather than something reachable by any respelling of this owner's own source.
